    What is this page?

    AI chatbots like ChatGPT normally run in giant data centers. You can also run a smaller one on your own computer, using the graphics card (GPU). The catch: a modest card like this one has only 6 GB of memory, and these AI models are big. Everything has to be squeezed in, and it can be slow.

    This page is a lab notebook. We changed the software that runs the AI (a program called llama.cpp), measured whether each change helped, and kept only what worked. The results are below, in plain terms first and technical details underneath.

    up to 4×Faster at readingHow quickly the AI takes in your question or document before it starts answering.
    up to 7×Faster at editing codeThe answer is exactly the same, it just arrives much sooner.
    +16–50%Faster at writingDepends on the model and how long the conversation is.
    ~60,000Words of memoryThe largest model can keep about this much text in mind at once (81,920 tokens) and still find facts in it.

    How to read this page

    1. Results shows each improvement as a before and after. Longer green bar means bigger gain. Click a row for the plain explanation.
    2. Long chats is about the AI's memory: how much text it can hold before the card runs out of room.
    3. What we changed lists the nine changes we kept.
    4. Tests lists what we tried, including the ideas that did not work.
    5. Coverage shows which tests were done on which models. For developers has commands and open tasks; skip it if you only want the story.

    Words you will see

    Model
    The AI itself, a very large file of numbers. Names like "7B" or "9B" mean 7 or 9 billion numbers. More is usually smarter, but bigger and slower.
    GPU / graphics card
    A chip that does huge amounts of simple math at once, which is just what AI needs. Much faster than the main processor for this job.
    CPU
    The computer's main processor. Slower for AI, but it has lots of ordinary memory (RAM) to spare.
    VRAM / memory
    The graphics card's own memory. Here only about 5.7 GB of it is usable. If the AI doesn't fit, part of it must run on the slower CPU.
    Token
    A chunk of text, roughly three quarters of a word. AI reads and writes in tokens.
    t/s (tokens per second)
    Speed. About 15 t/s is a comfortable reading speed; 50 t/s is very quick. Higher is better.
    Reading vs writing
    "Reading" (prompt processing) is the AI taking in your text. "Writing" (decoding or generating) is it producing the answer one token at a time. They have different speeds.
    Context
    How much text the AI can keep in mind at once: your question, the document, and its own answer. Longer context needs more memory.
    KV cache
    The AI's short-term notes about the conversation so far. It grows with every token, and it is what eats memory in long chats.
    Quantization (q4, q8)
    Storing numbers with less precision, like saving a photo at lower quality. The file shrinks and speeds up, with a small loss of accuracy that we measure.
    Perplexity
    A score of how well the AI predicts text. Lower is better. We use it to check that a speed-up did not make the AI worse.
    Kernel
    A small routine that runs on the graphics card to do one job, such as a bit of math. Picking a better one can make things much faster.
    Speculative decoding (ngram)
    Guessing the next several words in advance, then checking all the guesses at once. When the guesses are right, which is common when editing code, it saves a lot of time.
    Overclock
    Running the card faster than the factory setting. We only kept settings that gave identical answers and stayed cool.
    MiB
    A unit of memory. 1024 MiB is 1 GB.

    How much faster did things get?

    The longer the green bar, the bigger the gain. 2× means twice as fast. Click a row to see what it means.

    Where does the time go when the AI writes?

    Each bar is the time to produce one token, in milliseconds (shorter is faster), split by what the card is busy with. Rows are how much text came before (0K = empty, 15K = about 11,000 words). Pick a model.

    reading the model's numberslooking back over the chatother workcard waiting

    In plain terms: on the 7B and 4B models the card is already moving data almost as fast as its memory allows (83–89% of the limit), so the only way to go faster is to move less data. Longer chats slow the 7B because looking back over more text is extra work. The 9B spends most of its time with the card waiting for the part of the model that runs on the slower CPU.

    How long a conversation can the 9B model hold?

    The longer the text, the more memory the AI's notes (the KV cache) need. Each bar below is the card's memory use at that length. The red line is the most the card can give (5754 MiB). A bar that stays left of the line fits. "fail" means it ran out of room. The buttons try different ways of storing the notes: lower numbers like q4 are more compact.

    the AI model (3858)the chat notes (KV cache)working spacedesktop and other programs

    Longest verified conversation

    Biggest length where the AI, after reading a huge text with three secret codes hidden in it, correctly repeated all three. Peak and headroom are in MiB; t/s is writing speed, pp t/s is reading speed.

    A caveat: the pass rule says "3/3 hidden codes in jobs.py", but the probe plants three keys (ALPHA, BETA, GAMMA) and checks recall. Code asserts at long context are not recorded.

    What we will try next for long conversations

    1. Finish the forced vec-kernel run. At 48K the compute buffer is 55 MiB instead of 220: about 160 MiB of the 220 MiB deficit at 96K.
    2. imatrix + IQ3 FFN of the 9B. Needs weights under 3500 MiB; gate ΔPPL ≤ +0.08.
    3. Host KV (-nkvo 1) up to 128K; success is ≥ 6 t/s.

    Ideas we dropped, and why

    Run it yourself (for developers)

    cp local-tune/config/models.example.conf local-tune/config/models.conf
python3 local-tune/scripts/gateway.py &          # :8700
python3 local-tune/scripts/watch.py              # live view
python3 local-tune/scripts/suite.py run base
python3 local-tune/scripts/suite.py run next
python3 local-tune/scripts/assess.py next base
python3 local-tune/scripts/ctxprobe.py run <plan>
python3 local-tune/scripts/gpu-push.py apply     # after each reboot

    Our rule: a speed-up only counts if the AI still gives the same answers. Quality gates: correct first (backend ops, same text at temperature 0, perplexity within 0.5%), then fast. Under 3% is noise; use 3 repetitions.
